name: Cefalexin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Cefalexin (cephalexin) is over 90% excreted unchanged in urine within 8 hours. The US label (adults and children 15 years or older) needs no dose change above a creatinine clearance (CrCl) of 60 mL/min, caps the daily dose at 1 g at 30–59, and lowers it to 250 mg at longer intervals below 30. The label has too little information to recommend a dose on hemodialysis.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses CrCl (mL/min); bands at 60, 30, 15, 5 and 1. Applies to adults and children at least 15 years old.

bands.recommendation: CrCl 30–59: no dose change, but maximum daily dose 1 g (label).
CrCl 5–14, not on dialysis: 250 mg every 24 hours. CrCl 1–4, not on dialysis: 250 mg every 48 or 60 hours (label).

hd: Insufficient information to recommend a dose on hemodialysis (label). Specialist input.
pd: No peritoneal dialysis dosing in label. Specialist input.
crrt: Not in label; the cited CRRT review (Li 2020) gives no regimen for this drug. Specialist input.
dialyzable: Not established: the label says hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis has not been shown to help in overdose. Protein binding 10% to 15%.
monitoring: CrCl for dose; seizures with unadjusted doses in kidney impairment (label precautions); metformin levels if coadministered; diarrhea (CDAD).

pediatric.usual_dose: 25 to 50 mg/kg/day in divided doses (severe infections 50 to 100 mg/kg/day; otitis media 75 to 100 mg/kg/day) (label).

renal.recommendation: Children 15 years or older: use the adult CrCl table. Under 15 years: no kidney dosing in label; specialist input.
